policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Presence or absence of the article before Ἰησοῦς; English 'Jesus' is a bare proper name either way, and the only note is a greek_gloss on 'first'. Nothing in the ASV distinguishes.
Word order only. English syntax fixes 'ye shall be baptized in the Holy Spirit' whichever order the Greek prints; the note is an alternative_rendering on the preposition and cannot decide a reading.
ἠρώτων and ἐπηρώτων are both rendered 'asked'; the compound prefix leaves no trace in the English.
The ASV opens the sentence with a rendered connective, 'And he said unto them'; the omitting reading leaves asyndeton with nothing for 'And' to translate.
'ye shall be my witnesses' renders the genitive μου attributively; the dative μοι would give 'witnesses unto me', which is how the ASV marks a dative elsewhere in this chapter (1:26 note 'Or, unto').
Plural ἐσθήσεσι λευκαῖς against singular ἐσθῆτι λευκῇ; 'in white apparel' is a mass noun in English and carries no number, so the ASV does not distinguish.
βλέποντες and ἐμβλέποντες both yield 'looking into heaven'; the prefix is not represented in the English.
Word order only. 'they went up into the upper chamber' follows English verb-then-adjunct order under either reading.
The ASV names 'both Peter and John and James and Andrew' — John before James, matching Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἰάκωβος. This order is a sequence of proper names, which the English preserves.
The ASV has 'continued stedfastly in prayer' with no second noun; the added καὶ τῇ δεήσει would give 'and supplication', which is absent.
Μαριάμ and Μαρίᾳ are the indeclinable and declined forms of the same name; the ASV prints 'Mary' for either.
The ASV repeats the preposition in 'and with his brethren'; without σύν the brethren would simply join the preceding dative series and need no second 'with'.
'in the midst of the brethren' renders ἀδελφῶν; μαθητῶν would be 'disciples'.
ὡς and ὡσεί are both rendered 'about' before a numeral; the English does not separate them.
The ASV reads 'that the scripture should be fulfilled' with no demonstrative; the added ταύτην would give 'this scripture'.
Article present or absent before Ἰησοῦν; 'took Jesus' is the same English either way.
'he was numbered among us' renders ἐν ἡμῖν; the ASV renders σύν as 'with' consistently in this chapter ('with his brethren' 1:14, 'a witness with us' 1:22), so σὺν ἡμῖν would have given 'with us'.
'in their language' is fully accounted for by αὐτῶν, which both readings print; the ASV supplies no separate 'own' that would require ἰδίᾳ, and its absence does not exclude the redundant Greek.

Imperative λαβέτω against optative λάβοι. The ASV renders both third-person volitives with 'let' — compare 'Let his habitation be made desolate' for the imperative in the same verse — so 'His office let another take' does not distinguish the mood.

The ASV's 'all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and went out' uses the bare English relative, which serves a temporal antecedent whether or not the Greek relative carries ἐν; it neither requires nor excludes the preposition.
Word order only; 'must one become a witness with us' is the English order under either arrangement of σὺν ἡμῖν and γενέσθαι.
'to take the place in this ministry' renders τόπον, and the same word recurs in 'go to his own place'; κλῆρον would be 'lot' or 'portion', which the ASV uses at 1:17 and 1:26 for that word.
ἀπό and ἐκ are both rendered 'from which Judas fell away'; the English preposition does not separate them.
'they gave lots for them' with the note 'Or, unto' renders the dative αὐτοῖς; the genitive αὐτῶν would give 'their lots' and would leave the note without an object to attach to.
